vectors.name: empty-batch
vectors.note: A batch is an array of signals, so the empty batch is the empty array — one byte, and nothing after it.

vectors.name: one-empty-signal
vectors.note: A signal with no attributes is a legal signal, and distinct from a batch with no signals.

vectors.name: two-signals-keep-their-order
vectors.note: A batch is ordered (§6.3); only map keys are sorted, and only within a signal.

vectors.name: every-scalar-type
vectors.note: The whole scalar half of the §6.3 data model in one signal: the three admitted simple values, a binary64 float, a negative integer, text, and a byte string.

vectors.name: negative-zero-is-preserved
vectors.note: Rule 6 is a MUST in both directions: a decoder may neither reject this nor normalise it to +0.0, and re-encoding has to give back 0xfb8000000000000000 rather than 0xfb0000000000000000. A host that normalised would pass a value assertion and fail the re-encode.

vectors.name: i64-min
vectors.note: Major type 1 encodes -1-n, so i64::MIN is 0x3b followed by i64::MAX's bytes. A decoder that negated after widening to i64 overflows exactly here.

vectors.name: int-head-boundaries
vectors.note: The first value at each head width: 23 is the last immediate, 24 the first one-byte, 256 the first two-byte, 65536 the first four-byte, 2^32 the first eight-byte. One off-by-one in a shortest-head check fails here and nowhere else.

vectors.name: declared-length-is-delivered
vectors.note: Rule 11's accepting side: 24 elements need a one-byte length head, and every one of them is present. The rejecting side is the same head shape claiming what is not there.

vectors.name: keys-sort-by-content-not-encoding
vectors.note: The first RFC 8949 §4.2.1 deviation, from the accepting side. See deviations.json for the encoding a stock canonical encoder produces for this same signal.

vectors.name: non-ascii-key-sorts-by-utf8-bytes
vectors.note: Content bytes, not scalar values and not a collation: "ä" is 0xc3a4, so it follows "a". A host sorting by code point agrees here; one sorting by locale need not.

vectors.name: control-characters-are-ordinary-text
vectors.note: Text is a Unicode scalar sequence; nothing in §6.3 excludes the C0 range, and a decoder that escaped or refused it would not round-trip.

vectors.name: float-fraction-and-large-magnitude
vectors.note: Rule 5's accepting side: every finite binary64 is admitted, including magnitudes a binary32 could not carry — which is also why rule 4 cannot be met by narrowing.

vectors.name: nesting-within-any-conforming-bound
vectors.note: Sixteen levels, well inside EXPR §9's MAX_DEPTH floor, so every conforming host accepts this whatever bound it configures. The vector deliberately does not sit at the bound: §6.3.1 fixes that the depth is bounded, not where one level is counted, and a vector pinning that off-by-one would fail a host counting the batch array as a level.
